The chestnut-oak type is found in the Bearwallow Gorge, the Toxaway Gorge above 2,000 feet, and the Chattooga Gorge. It occurs on east and north-facing slopes at lower elevations; at higher elevations it occurs continuously. Chestnut oak is the principal species with red oak becoming more important at higher elevations. The most common associated species are red maple, scarlet oak (Quercus coccinea), and sourwood (Table 2-3). Most stands have a very dense ericaceous shrub stratum dominated by mountain laurel and rhododendron (R. maximum and R. carolinianum). The herbaceous understory is usually sparse with galax (Galax aphylla) common.
The mixed oak-hickory community occurs on the drier, open south- and west-facing slopes in the lower portion of the gorges. The dominant tree in this community is the white oak (often codominant with chestnut oak). Black and scarlet oaks appear also as dominants or codominants. Other species found in the canopy include red maple, black locust (Robinia pseudo-acacia), and black gum. Understory dominants are sourwood and dogwood. The shrub layer is composed almost exclusively of ericaceous species with mountain laurel and blueberry (Vaccinium vacillans and V. stamineum).
2.2.1.5 Pine-Dominated Types
The dry, open ridges in the gorges are dominated by pine. The open canopy is dominated by pitch pine, Virginia pine, and shortleaf pine (Pinus echinata). The understory is comprised of hardwood tree species. Generally, pine communities are more common at low elevations and are best developed on extremely narrow ridges, highly exposed sites above the gorges, and slopes of southeasterly to southwesterly exposure.
The pine community type is found at elevations from 1,900 to 2,600 feet, and is characterized by stands having twice the abundance of hardwoods. This community is found on the driest ridges below elevation 2,800 feet. Associated hardwoods include scarlet and chestnut oak, black gum, and red maple. The herbaceous cover is dominated by scattered patches of mountain laurel and blueberry. Chimaphila maculata and Uvularia pudica are characteristic of the herbaceous layer.
